note: Rows the repaired reading reads otherwise than their source-reviewed expectation, pinned by their exact output with the reason. A change that fixes one fails its pin and must update this file deliberately.

AN1.reason: interpretation 42: a label no section governs is asked, never sent by itself, also where it is the only date-of-service label (an accepted over-ask: a member's answer equal to it is taken)

AN2.reason: as AN1, in PDF lines: the only date-of-service label after the plan is asked, never sent by itself; a member's answer equal to it is taken

AN3.reason: as AN1, under another neutral heading: the only date-of-service label after the plan is asked, never sent by itself; a member's answer equal to it is taken

AN4.reason: as AN3, in PDF lines: the only date-of-service label after the plan is asked, never sent by itself; a member's answer equal to it is taken

C5.reason: as AN1: the procedure report's only labelled date stands in a billing block after its recommendations

HN1.reason: as AN1: the only date-of-service label stands under a neutral heading after a history section

HC6.reason: pre-existing (the head reads the same): an "Outside records" block's "Procedure: EGD" heading opens a procedure section, so its date reads as the note's own and conflicts with the header; part 3 covers only a procedure section after a plan

HC7.reason: pre-existing (the head reads the same): a results table outside any history section; its row date speaks against the header

PC4.reason: B4 (interpretation 42) asks a procedure date field in a plan with no block heading unless the item before it names a later occurrence; "Colonoscopy with possible polypectomy." names the planned service but no later-occurrence word (an over-ask, never a send)

PG2.reason: part 3 asks the planned procedure's date beside the visit's own; the head reads the same conflict (part 3 asks, it does not silence)

R-X3-only.reason: X3: a label broken over two lines is a form the installed revision never read (rule N7), so the only one is asked, never sent by itself; a member's answer equal to it is taken

R-X3-no-separator.reason: X3 requires the separator on the second line (interpretation 42's X3); without it the broken label is unread, as at the head, and the header date is sent

R-RC5-bare-follow-up.reason: RC5 reads only a follow-up title no heading list holds; a bare "Follow-up" is the section reader's own plan heading, so its header stays governed (asked, as at the head)

R-RC5-colon.reason: RC5 reads only a colon-less title; "Hepatology follow-up:" is a bare plan label, so its header stays governed (asked, as at the head)

R-RC6-pos-only.reason: RC6: a setting label the plan no longer governs speaks against the note's own setting but is never the setting by itself; alone it stays unread as at the head (the setting is asked and a member's answer taken)
